source.title: Open Problems About Sumsets in Finite Abelian Groups: Minimum Sizes and Critical Numbers

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, and let A={a1,...,am} be an m-element subset of G. For a positive integer h, define the h-fold sumset hA to be the set of all sums λ1a1+...+λm am with nonnegative integer coefficients λ1,...,λm whose total is h, and define ρ(G,m,h) as the minimum of |hA| over all m-element subsets A of G. If p is the smallest prime divisor of n and m ≤ p < hm - h + 1, is it true that ρ(G,m,h)=p and that an m-element subset A satisfies |hA|=p if and only if A is contained in a coset of a subgroup H of G with |H|=p?
accepted.context_brief: Direct and inverse problem for ordinary h-fold sumsets

evidence.quote: the h-fold sumset: hA = {Σ_i=1^m λ_i ai | λ1,...,λm ∈ N0, Σ_i=1^m λi = h}
ρ (G, m, h) = min{|hA| | A ⊆ G, |A| = m}

Conjecture 3 Let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume that m ≤ p < hm − h + 1. Then for an m-subset A of G we have |hA| = ρ (G, m, h) = p if, and only if, A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G with |H| = p.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and for an m-element subset A={a1,...,am} define hA as the set of all sums λ1a1+...+λm am with nonnegative integer coefficients summing to h. Define ρ(G,m,h) as the minimum possible value of |hA| over all m-element subsets A of G. In the boundary case p = hm - h + 1, classify all m-element subsets A of G for which |hA|=ρ(G,m,h). In particular, determine all extremal subsets beyond the known possibilities of arithmetic progressions of length m and m-subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of order p.

evidence.quote: the h-fold sumset: hA = {Σ_i=1^m λ_i ai | λ1,...,λm ∈ N0, Σ_i=1^m λi = h}
ρ (G, m, h) = min{|hA| | A ⊆ G, |A| = m}

This leaves the case when p = hm − h + 1, where arithmetic progressions of length m and m-subsets in a coset of a subgroup of order p are two of several possibilities. It may be an interesting problem to classify all such subsets.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, and let A={a1,...,am} be an m-element subset of G. For a positive integer h, define the h-fold restricted sumset h^A as the set of all sums λ1a1+...+λm am where each λi is either 0 or 1 and the coefficients sum to h; equivalently, h^A is the set of sums of h distinct elements of A. Let ρ^(G,m,h) be the minimum of |h^A| over all m-element subsets A of G. If p is the smallest prime divisor of n and h < m ≤ p, must ρ^(G,m,h) equal min{p, hm - h^2 + 1}?
accepted.context_brief: Restricted sumset formula when m ≤ p

evidence.quote: the h-fold restricted sumset: hˆA = {Σ_i=1^m λ_i ai | λ1,...,λm ∈ {0, 1}, Σ_i=1^m λi = h}
ρˆ(G, m, h) = min{|hˆA| | A ⊆ G, |A| = m}
Conjecture 6 If p is the smallest prime divisor of n and h < m ≤ p, then ρˆ(G, m, h) = min{p, hm − h2 + 1}.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, and for an m-element subset A={a1,...,am} define h^A as the set of sums of h distinct elements of A. Let p be the smallest prime divisor of n. Suppose 2 ≤ h ≤ m - 2 and p > hm - h^2 + 1. Classify the m-element subsets A of G for which |h^A| has the minimum value hm - h^2 + 1. Is it true that equality occurs if and only if either h=2, m=4, and A={a, a+g1, a+g2, a+g1+g2} for some a,g1,g2 in G, or A is an arithmetic progression in G?
accepted.context_brief: Inverse problem for restricted sumsets above the prime threshold

evidence.quote: the h-fold restricted sumset: hˆA = {Σ_i=1^m λ_i ai | λ1,...,λm ∈ {0, 1}, Σ_i=1^m λi = h}

Conjecture 7 Let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume that 2 ≤ h ≤ m − 2 and p > hm − h2 + 1. Then for an m-subset A of G we have |hˆA| = hm − h2 + 1 if, and only if, h = 2, m = 4, and A = {a, a + g1, a + g2, a + g1 + g2} for some a, g1 , g2 ∈ G, or A is an arithmetic progression in G.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, and for an m-element subset A={a1,...,am} define h^A as the set of sums of h distinct elements of A. Let p be the smallest prime divisor of n. If m ≤ p < hm - h^2 + 1, is it true that an m-element subset A satisfies |h^A|=p if and only if A is contained in a coset of a subgroup H of G with |H|=p?
accepted.context_brief: Inverse problem for restricted sumsets at size p

evidence.quote: the h-fold restricted sumset: hˆA = {Σ_i=1^m λ_i ai | λ1,...,λm ∈ {0, 1}, Σ_i=1^m λi = h}

Conjecture 8 Let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume that m ≤ p < hm − h2 + 1. Then for an m-subset A of G we have |hˆA| = p if, and only if, A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G with |H| = p.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, and let A={a1,...,am} be an m-element subset of G. For h=2, define the ordinary sumset 2A using nonnegative integer coefficients with total 2, and define the signed sumset 2±A using integer coefficients λ1,...,λm with |λ1|+...+|λm|=2. Let ρ(G,m,2) and ρ±(G,m,2) be the minimum possible sizes of these two sumsets over all m-element subsets A of G. Is it true that ρ±(G,m,2) and ρ(G,m,2) differ for fewer than n/4 values of m?
accepted.context_brief: Frequency of disagreement for two-fold signed sumsets

evidence.quote: h± A = {Σ_i=1^m λ_i ai | λ1,...,λm ∈ Z, Σ_i=1^m |λ_i| = h}.
ρ± (G, m, h) = min{|h± A| | A ⊆ G, |A| = m}
Conjecture 13 For any abelian group of order n, ρ± (G, m, 2) and ρ (G, m, 2) disagree for fewer than n/4 values of m.

accepted.question_text: For the cyclic group Z_n, define the restricted 3-fold sumset 3^A of a subset A as the set of all sums of three distinct elements of A. Define the restricted 3-critical number χ^(Z_n,3) as the least integer m such that 3^A=Z_n for every m-element subset A of Z_n. Are the following lower bounds always sharp for n≥16? If n has a prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3 and p is the smallest such divisor, then χ^(Z_n,3) should equal (1+1/p)n/3+3 when n=p, (1+1/p)n/3+2 when n=3p, and (1+1/p)n/3+1 otherwise. If n has no prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3, then χ^(Z_n,3) should equal floor(n/3)+4 when 9 divides n and floor(n/3)+3 otherwise.
accepted.context_brief: Sharpness of lower bounds for restricted 3-critical numbers

evidence.quote: the h-fold restricted sumset: hˆA = {Σ_i=1^m λ_i ai | λ1,...,λm ∈ {0, 1}, Σ_i=1^m λi = h}
Given G and h, we define the h-critical number χ (G, h) as the least integer m for which hA = G holds for all m-subsets A of G; we define χˆ(G, h) and χ± (G, h) analogously.
We also believe that, actually, equality holds above for all n—this is certainly the case if n is even or prime; we have verified this (by computer) for all n ≤ 50.

needs_review.question_text_raw: For positive integers n, m, and h, is the minimum size of the h-fold restricted sumset in the cyclic group Z_n exactly min{u_hat(n,m,h), w_hat(n,m,h)}? Equivalently, does rho_hat(Z_n,m,h) always equal the better of the two explicit upper bounds coming from the constructions A_d(n,m) and B_d(n,m)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5 For all n, m, and h, we have ρˆ(Zn , m, h) = min{uˆ(n, m, h), wˆ(n, m, h)}.

needs_review.question_text_raw: For every finite abelian group G, every positive integer m, and every h >= 3, does the minimum size of the h-fold signed sumset equal the explicit upper bound u_plusminus(G,m,h)? Equivalently, is rho_plusminus(G,m,h)=u_plusminus(G,m,h) always true for signed sumsets with at least three terms?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10 (Bajnok and Matzke [9]) For all G, m, and h ≥ 3, we have ρ± (G, m, h) = u± (G, m, h).

Let p be an odd prime and consider the elementary abelian group Z_p^r. Set delta=0 when p-1 is divisible by h and delta=1 otherwise. Let k be the largest integer with p^k+delta <= hm-h+1, and let q be the largest integer with (hq+1)p^k+delta <= hm-h+1. If h

(q+1)p^k, must rho_plusminus(Z_p^r,m,h)>rho(Z_p^r,m,h)?

evidence.quote: First, set k equal to the largest integer for which pk + δ ≤ hm − h + 1, where δ = 0 if p − 1 is divisible by h and δ = 1 otherwise.
Conjecture 12 (Bajnok and Matzke [10]) If h < p and m > (q + 1)pk with k and q defined as above, then ρ± (Zrp , m, h) > ρ (Zrp , m, h).

needs_review.question_text_raw: Classify exactly when symmetric, near-symmetric, and asymmetric m-subsets of a finite abelian group yield signed sumsets of minimum possible size.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, it would be interesting to know exactly when each of the three types of sets just described yields a signed sumset of minimum size.

needs_review.question_text_raw: For all positive integers n and m <= n, is the minimum size of the restricted sumset with an arbitrary number of terms in the cyclic group Z_n equal to the explicit bound u(n,m,N_0)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 15 For all positive integers n and m ≤ n, we have ρˆ(Zn , m, N0 ) = u(n, m, N0 ).

evidence.quote: there is a positive integer p0 so that if p > p0 is prime and A ⊆ Z p has size χˆ(Z p , N0 ) − 1 = ⌊2 p − 2⌋, then Σ A 6= Z p if, and only if, there is a nonzero element b ∈ Z p for which ||b · A|| ≤ p − 2.
